gap: None of the results ChatGPT got say what a timer plug costs to run on its own: using Brian Dorey's measured 0.56 W idle and 1.22 W with the relay on, that comes to about $0.89 to $1.94 per plug per year at the August 2026 US average rate of 18.16¢/kWh. Over five years that is roughly what each plug costs to buy.
standout_why: I opened the two cited TP-Link/Tapo timer FAQs (tp-link.com/us/support/faq/947 and tapo.com/us/faq/83) and four top-ranked roundups: stackandvalue, techgearden, rottenwifi and pickedproperly. None gives a standby or idle wattage, a yearly running cost, or a schedule limit, except stackandvalue's single line for the Tapo P115: 'Up to 32 schedules per plug'. Stackandvalue already does price per plug, so that derivation isn't new. The standby-cost figure is new, but the only named measurement I found is of an older Kasa HS10x, not of ChatGPT's picks. It can't rank the candidates against each other, so it isn't a 3.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick. A Wi-Fi timer plug's own draw is small: under $2 a year even with the relay held on, and a 4-pack left on all the time is under about $8 a year. So for 'smart plug with timer', choose on timer features, not on running cost. On features, the cited Tapo FAQ lists Auto-Off only for Kasa EP40M, KP125M, EP25 V2 and all Tapo plugs. The Kasa EP10, which ChatGPT called 'best for simple timers', isn't on that list. A shopper who wants an automatic shut-off every time the plug turns on should get a Tapo plug or the EP25 V2 instead.
